segments.text: This is Type Staircase, one of the free templates on Sycamore.
It builds one sentence a word at a time, and every new word steps down and to the right, like it's walking down a flight of stairs.
Look at the sizing. The words that carry the point, like content and system, come in big. The little connecting words stay small, so your eye jumps straight to what matters.
Every word slides in out of a soft blur, and the camera keeps following the newest one, so the older words drift off the left edge.
Here's the thing. I didn't animate any of this by hand. It came from one prompt.
And you can make your own version of it with Claude Code. Here's how.
Go to sycamore dot to slash motion, and open Type Staircase.
Under the preview there's a copy prompt button. That copies the whole prompt, the one that built this exact animation.
It spells out everything. The sizes, the timing of every word, the easing, and the camera move. It's almost two thousand words.
Now open Claude Code and paste it in.
Then tell it what to change. I asked for a dark background, an orange accent, and my own sentence.
Hit send, and let it work. This one took about ten minutes.
And here's what came back. Same staircase, same timing, but it's mine now.
That's the whole trick. The prompt does the heavy lifting, and Claude Code does the rest. Every template on the site comes with one.
